rows.name: Clear goal and feedback
rows.note: I knew the next floor I wanted, but I initially mistook the ration button's 'ok $650' for a completed purchase and only later confirmed it.

rows.name: Interesting decisions
rows.note: I accepted 'D23 38→0%' to try a safe cash farm for the overnight return, and would make that choice again only when money mattered more than a new floor. Named lapse: The first few town purchases and sends had little room for a defensible alternative.

rows.name: Mastery curve
rows.note: I can now put a specific threat ahead of the nearest enemy, and the next run actually showed 'hit drain wraith' before those enemies could keep shaving my maximum health. Named lapse: The early editor lock delayed independent row practice, and later changes mixed gear, traits and rows so their individual effects were not always separable.

rows.name: Tension, risk and release
rows.note: The Master fight caught me at '6/42 hp' while new carry was at risk, and the final healing recovery made its defeat a relief. Named lapse: Once the mail improved, long ordinary stretches consisted mostly of harmless blocked blows.

rows.name: Feel and juice
rows.note: Menu selections answered promptly and big hit numbers were easy to see, but repeated 'REST ✗ NOT SAFE' bubbles kept drawing my eye away from the actual blows; I could not listen to audio.

rows.name: Surprise and variety
rows.note: The learned 'iron golem · reflects melee' made me keep the reflector tactic for the foundry instead of treating every enemy as another nearest-target fight. Named lapse: Conjurers, their blades and familiar goblin encounters repeated extensively between the new walls.

rows.name: Expression and identity
rows.note: My adventurer is a guarded rogue who tries an unknown scroll in danger and hunts draining enemies first, with '2/4 rules' sitting above the supplied packages. Named lapse: Early custom rows were locked; most of the eventual priority list remained supplied packages or automatic lessons.

rows.name: Story to tell
rows.note: After 'grudge: Ulak the ghoul' marked Jora's killer, I sent Kael with draining enemies first, watched him kill Ulak and the Lich, and saw him survive the Master before reaching D25. Named lapse: Most ordinary report reels were short damage-and-bank summaries without a comparable turn.

rows.name: Flow and pacing
rows.note: The 'D9–12 swift · 100%' fold cut familiar travel, but later ordinary fights still repeated for minutes; my return visits gave distinct preparation choices while the expanded ledgers took sustained reading.

rows.name: Fairness and legibility of failure
rows.note: Jora lost because I left nearest attacks ahead of the draining enemy while healing was empty and 'to corridor vs 3+ · no path ← foes hold the way' ruled out my escape plan. Named lapse: The useful explanation was behind an expanded, long trace; the compact death view did not itself tell me the whole missed escape sequence.

rows.name: Autonomy and exploration
rows.note: I switched away from the starting fighter to a rogue and later pursued safe cash before depth, even though the town still pointed me toward 'Goal D23'.

rows.name: Collection and progression
rows.note: The rogue's levels, bigger pack and new floor vocabulary stayed available between heirs, and 'scout · sent 10' meant I no longer had to initiate every expedition myself. Named lapse: Collected set pieces were announced while the report still said set log 0/3, leaving that persistent collection layer unclear.

rows.name: Atmosphere and audiovisual appeal
rows.note: Torchlit stone, parchment reports and the line 'Slag with silver in it.' made the dungeon inviting to look at, although packed grey figures and oversized control panels sometimes obscured the scene; audio is unassessed. Named lapse: Overlapping grey figures and the large control panel sometimes hid the action beneath labels.

rows.name: Return payoff (idle)
rows.note: After four hours I came back to the Lich beaten, an heir lost and 'apprentice · +2 steps → pack 5', so I studied the gas death and changed preparation rather than wishing I had stayed to tap sends. Named lapse: The drill/legacy/forge reward menu repeated across absences even when the underlying expedition history differed.

rows.name: Attribution of the agent's play (idle)
rows.note: I credit my extra healing slot for the last 'heal potion · +21 HP' in the Master fight, while the automatic reflector package and personality changes mean I cannot claim every winning blow as my own authored instruction. Named lapse: Automatic personality and reflector changes contributed to wins I could not fully separate from my own rows.
